newsitem.title: INDIA: India 96/97 sugar output seen at 14 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: India 96/97 sugar output seen at 14 mln tonnes.

text.p: India's sugar output in 1996/97 (October-September) is expected to be about 14 million tonnes compared with 16.5 million last year, Shanti Lal Jain, director general of Indian Sugar Mills Association (ISMA) told Reuters on Thursday.
"We expect the current season sugar output to be around 14 million tonnes," Jain told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Jain said the per acre yield for sugarcane had decreased by about 15-17 percent across the country, and this would contribute to a dip in sugar output.
There had also been a delay in the start of crushing operations, Jain said.

"But this is not a worrisome development because we have begun the year with all time record carry-forward stocks of eight million tonnes which is five million higher than the normal carry over stocks of three million," Jain said.
"Eventually, we will still be having some surplus stocks, notwithstanding the likely drop in production this year," he said.
